speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with shortness of breath, increased abdominal girth, and a large ovarian mass. To better understand your condition, have you been experiencing any pain in your abdomen or pelvis?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Malignant Ovarian Tumor (Epithelial) with Malignant Ascites and Pleural Effusion.

The combination of a large ovarian mass, shortness of breath, and increased abdominal girth in a 40-year-old woman is highly suggestive of advanced ovarian cancer causing both ascites and a pleural effusion. This diagnosis is supported by the clinical presentation of a large mass and respiratory compromise.
